CHIEF COMPLAINT
Asthma difficulty with sports and mood concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient has asthma and attempted to join water polo. Reports difficulty breathing during sports, requiring breaks and use of albuterol inhaler. Symptoms primarily triggered by aerobic activities such as sports and running. Also triggered by smoke exposure. When symptomatic, describes phlegm accumulation in throat, cough, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness. Uses 2 puffs of albuterol inhaler, which alleviates symptoms within about 15 minutes but patient still requires sitting down to breathe. Notes shakiness as a side effect of the inhaler. Denies nighttime symptoms. Not currently on daily asthma medications; only uses albuterol as-needed. Reports symptoms occur approximately every time with aerobic activity. Additionally reports mood concerns including stress, sadness, lack of motivation, and fatigue. Attributes mood symptoms to school pressure including studying for SATs and taking AP classes. Reports that friends invite him out but prefers to stay home. States mood symptoms are new, started this year.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Asthma symptoms with exertion and smoke exposure. Denies nighttime symptoms. Reports fatigue.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Asthma

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler, 2 puffs as needed

ALLERGIES
Seasonal allergies

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Student studying for SATs and taking AP classes. Attempted to participate in water polo. Has social activities with friends. Exposed to secondhand smoke from others.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart: Sounds good.
Lungs: Sound good.
Eyes: Normal.
Ears: Fluid noted.
Throat: Normal, no tonsils.
Abdomen: Normal on auscultation and palpation.
Reflexes: Normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Asthma, exercise-induced: Suspected allergic component. Initiated daily Singulair. Continue albuterol inhaler as needed for acute symptoms. Counseled that shakiness is expected side effect of albuterol; continue to rest after use. Expect improvement within one month. Return for follow-up in 6 weeks.

2. Mood concerns: New-onset sadness, lack of motivation, and fatigue related to school stress. Referred to therapy. Depression screening questionnaires to be completed. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
